# Game model (7 levels, click-only)

## Interface
- Only ACTION6 (click) is available. Coordinates are 512x512.
- Board = 64x64 grid of 8px cells. Row 0 (y 0-7) is a PINK budget bar: 64 segments,
  one consumed per action (drains from one end). It refills at each new level.
- Progress {completed}/7 increments when a level's goal is met.

## Elements
- #666666 gray = "material" filling a chamber from one side.
- #FFFFFF white = empty part of a chamber.
- #000000 black horizontal BAR = divider between two vertically stacked chambers.
  The bar spans from the material side and ends partway.
- #1E93FF blue 4x4 block = BUTTON, sits in the WHITE (empty) part of a chamber,
  directly adjacent (above or below) to a bar.
- Marker color (yellow lvl1 / green lvl2): one 2-cell-wide marker painted on a BAR
  (the target column) and one marker on the PLAYER piece.
- PLAYER piece: T/arrow-shaped piece riding on the leading edge of the material in
  one chamber; its 2-wide colored marker is the outermost 2 columns of that material.

## Mechanics (verified)
- Clicking a blue button: the chamber CONTAINING that button loses 4 cells of
  material; the chamber on the OTHER side of the adjacent bar gains 4 cells.
  Total material is conserved.
- The player piece rides the material edge, so it shifts 4 cells per transfer.
- Clicks that do not land on a blue button do nothing but still consume 1 budget
  segment.

## Goal
Move material between chambers so the PLAYER's marker ends up in the same columns
as the marker painted on the bar. Then the level completes.

## Planning
- Compute required change in the player's chamber (4 cells per click), and route
  the surplus/deficit through neighbouring chambers. Chambers appear to have a
  capacity limit (a chamber probably cannot fully bury its own button), so offload
  first when a receiving chamber is near full.

# Game model (7 levels, click-only)

## Interface
- Only ACTION6 (click), coordinates in 512x512. Board = 64x64 grid of 8px cells.
- Row 0 (or a strip) is a PINK budget bar of 64 segments; 1 consumed per action.
  It refills at each new level. Level completion is automatic when the goal holds.

## Layout
A level is a set of parallel CHAMBERS separated by straight BARS (black).
- Chambers can be stacked vertically (bars horizontal) or side by side (bars vertical).
- Each chamber is filled with gray MATERIAL from one end; WHITE is the empty part.
  Define a chamber's "level" = number of filled rows/cols (its surface position).
- Blue 4x4/3x3/2x2 BUTTONS sit in the white part of a chamber, flush against a bar.
  A bar may have a button on each side, or none (none => no transfer across it).
- PLAYER piece: T/arrow shape hanging on the material surface, with a colored MARKER
  strip exactly at the surface. TARGET = a same-colored marker painted on a BAR.

## Mechanics (verified)
- Clicking a button: its own chamber loses N units of material, the chamber on the
  other side of the adjacent bar gains N.  N = BAR THICKNESS in cells
  (lvl1/2 bars 4 cells -> N=4; lvl3 bars 2 -> N=2; lvl4 bars 3 -> N=3).
- Total material is conserved within each group of chambers linked by buttons.
- A chamber may fill completely (covering its own buttons, which stay clickable-looking
  but the chamber is then at max). Max level = full chamber length.
- Minimum level: the surface may not retreat past the top/near end of an adjacent bar
  (otherwise the chambers would merge).
- Clicks not on a button/active doorway do nothing but still cost 1 budget segment.

## Doorways (from level 4)
- A LIGHT-GRAY (#CCCCCC) segment inside a bar is a DOORWAY spanning a range of rows.
- When the two chambers adjacent to that bar have EQUAL surface levels AND that level
  lies inside the doorway range, the doorway lights up ORANGE.
- Clicking the orange doorway moves the PLAYER to the other chamber.

## Goal
Bring the player's marker to the same rows/cols as the matching colored marker painted
on a bar (crossing doorways as needed). Then the level completes.

## Method
1. Read the board into: chamber extents, bar positions/thickness, doorway ranges,
   button positions, each chamber's level, player position, target position.
2. Solve the flow problem (levels change by N per click, totals conserved per group,
   respect min/max), then order clicks so no chamber overflows/underflows.

# Game model — COMPLETED (7/7 levels, WIN at turn 180)

## Interface
- Only ACTION6 (click), coordinates in the 512x512 frame. Board = 64x64 grid of 8px cells.
- A PINK strip (usually row 0) is a 64-segment budget bar; every action consumes one
  segment. It refills at each new level. Levels complete automatically when solved.

## Layout grammar
Parallel CHAMBERS separated by straight BARS (black). Orientation varies per level
(horizontal bars/stacked chambers, vertical bars/side-by-side, or mixed T/cross layouts).
- Each chamber is filled with gray MATERIAL from one fixed end; the rest is WHITE.
  "level" = number of filled rows/cols; the LEADING EDGE is the last filled row/col.
- Blue BUTTONS (square, same thickness as the bar) sit flush against a bar, at the
  white end of a chamber. A bar with no buttons permits no transfers.
  Buttons are drawn on top and remain CLICKABLE even when buried by material.
- PLAYER: T/arrow piece riding the leading edge, with a colored MARKER strip exactly at
  the leading edge (marker width = 3 units, thickness = 1 unit).
- TARGET: a same-colored marker painted on a BAR; solve by putting the player's marker
  at those rows/cols.

## Mechanics (all verified)
- Click a button => its own chamber loses N units; the chamber on the other side of the
  adjacent bar gains N.  N = BAR THICKNESS in cells (4, 2, 3, 3, 3, 2 across levels).
- Material is conserved within each group of chambers linked by buttons.
- Max level = the full chamber length (it may bury its own buttons).
- Min level: the leading edge may not retreat past the near END of an adjacent bar
  (where the bar stops, the two chambers merge).
- Non-button, non-doorway clicks do nothing but still cost a budget segment.

## Doorways
- A LIGHT-GRAY (#CCCCCC) segment inside a bar spans a range of rows/cols.
- It turns ORANGE only when BOTH adjacent chambers' leading edge sits exactly at the
  doorway's FAR end (the end away from the material anchor) — i.e. material exactly
  covers the doorway on both sides. Merely being inside the range is NOT enough.
- Clicking an orange doorway moves the player across. If BOTH chambers hold a player,
  one click SWAPS them.

## Solving method
1. Read the board: chamber extents/anchors/levels, bar positions + thickness, doorway
   ranges, button positions, player and target positions.
2. Note the invariants: totals per linked group, and each chamber's level mod N.
   Use them to check which target chamber is even feasible (capacity + parity).
3. Fix the required level at every crossing event (doorway far end) and the final
   levels, then solve the flow; order clicks so no chamber over/underflows.
   Cost is dominated by the total variation of the hub chamber's level.

[After action · message]
Completed the game — **WIN, 7/7 levels**.

## What the game turned out to be

A hydraulic/flow puzzle. Each level is a set of chambers separated by black bars; each chamber is filled with gray "material" from one end, and blue buttons pump a fixed quantity (= the bar's thickness) from their own chamber to the chamber on the other side of the adjacent bar. A small player piece rides the material's leading edge, and the goal is to line its colored marker up with the matching marker painted on a bar.

## Key discoveries along the way

- **Turn 1–3 were wasted probes** — clicking the player and empty space does nothing but still burns budget. The blue squares were the actual controls.
- **Transfer size = bar thickness** (4, 2, 3, 3, 3, 2 across levels) — inferred after level 3's arithmetic only closed with a 2-unit step, and later confirmed directly.
- **Level 3's feasibility only worked if chambers can fill completely over their own buttons** — which then proved true, and buried buttons stay clickable (critical for level 6, where the only viable route required one).
- **Doorway rule correction (level 5):** I first assumed "equal levels anywhere inside the light-gray segment." That failed a live test at level 37, and the corrected rule — the material must exactly cover the whole doorway on both sides — held for every crossing afterward.
- **Doorways swap two players in one click**, which I exploited in levels 5 and 7.

The hardest levels were solved as flow problems with conservation, capacity, and mod-N parity constraints: level 5 required two players to fully swap across four chambers (37 clicks), and level 7 routed three players through a central hub (49 clicks), both comfortably inside the 64-action budget.
